intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is caused by homozygous mutation in the syntaxin-11 gene (STX11; 605014) on chromosome 6q24.2.

checks.evidence_quote: we found homozygous mutations in STX11 in five consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds
checks.explanation: The paper identifies homozygous STX11 mutations as the cause of the FHL type-4 locus.

paragraphs.text: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is an autosomal recessive form of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). It presents in infancy or childhood with fever, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperferritinemia. Patients have defective natural killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity and degranulation (Muller et al., 2014). Compared with other forms of FHL, STX11 mutations have been associated with a milder course that can include prolonged remissions without specific treatment (Rudd et al., 2006).

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) reported 3 children from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families who presented with HLH. Patient A, a boy, presented at 2 months of age with fever, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia (hemoglobin 55 g/L), neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperferritinemia. Patient B, a boy, presented at 5 years of age with the same features (hemoglobin 71 g/L). Hemophagocytosis and neurologic manifestations were absent in both boys. Patient C, a girl, presented at 48 months of age with a hyperinflammatory syndrome. All 3 patients had deficient NK cell activity and degranulation.

paragraphs.text: zur Stadt et al. (2005) screened positional candidate genes in a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred linked to 6q24. In affected children they found a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. They then found homozygous STX11 mutations in 5 consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds. Two families had the 5-bp deletion, 1 family had a 19.2-kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2), and 2 families had a nonsense mutation causing a premature stop codon in the C-terminal end of the protein. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the 5-bp deletion.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) sequenced the coding regions and splice sites of UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2 in 3 children with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families. All 3 were homozygous for a novel missense mutation in the Habc domain of STX11, c.173T-C, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution. The parents were heterozygous for the mutation and had no recorded history of inflammatory disease. Patient A was also heterozygous for a rare UNC13D variant, c.811C-T (P271S), inherited from the father, and homozygous for an uncommon UNC13D variant, c.2782C-T (R928C). The authors suggested that these UNC13D variants might contribute to the severity of his disease. Syntaxin-11 levels were greatly reduced in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patient C. Her lymphokine-activated killer (LAK) cells showed a selective loss of syntaxin-11 expression, whereas Munc18-2 expression was similar to that of controls.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) found defective NK cell cytotoxicity and degranulation in patients homozygous for the STX11 L58P mutation, with normal expression of perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a. IL-2 stimulation partly restored both cytotoxicity and degranulation. In HEK-293T cells, the syntaxin-11 L58P mutant and an N-peptide R4A mutant were expressed at wildtype levels but did not bind Munc18-2. In contrast, the C-terminal Q268X FHL4 mutant still bound Munc18-2. The authors proposed that loss of Munc18-2 binding may destabilize syntaxin-11, which would explain its low expression in patient cells.

paragraphs.text: Locatelli et al. (2020) conducted an open-label, single-group phase 2-3 study of emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, given with dexamethasone. The 34 patients were aged 18 years or younger and had primary HLH; 27 had been treated previously and 7 had not. Among previously treated patients, 63% had a response, compared with a prespecified null hypothesis of 40%. Seventy percent of these patients proceeded to transplantation, and 74% were alive at the last observation. Emapalumab was not associated with any organ toxicity. Severe infections developed in 10 patients during treatment, and emapalumab was stopped in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) studied 3 children with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families: 2 boys who presented at 2 months and 5 years of age and a girl who presented at 48 months. All 3 were homozygous for a c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in the Habc domain. Their unaffected parents were heterozygous. NK cell cytotoxicity and degranulation were deficient in the patients. Syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and LAK cells from patient C. In HEK-293T cells, the L58P mutant was expressed at wildtype levels but did not bind Munc18-2. One patient also carried UNC13D variants (P271S heterozygous and R928C homozygous), which the authors suggested might contribute to the severity of his disease.
